$comment: What tools/status.mjs (npm run status) can't read from the repository. Everything else in docs/status.md comes from the lesson files, lessons.ts, review-queue.json and pending-photos.json.

Per course: student (default for its lessons: done | pending), gemini ('never' = no copy edit yet and not queued; leave out when the review queue says it all), geminiNote, facts (pending | 'done YYYY-MM-DD ...'), expectsPhotos (true: a written lesson with no photo counts as awaiting photos), note (one line under the course heading), planned (lessons in an outline that are not yet in lessons.ts: { id, n, code, title, teaches, branch }). A course with no folder yet (only an outline) is listed by its key with a title, an order and its planned lessons, each with a code and a branch title.

Per lesson, under lessons.<id>: student, facts, gemini ('done' to clear a course-wide 'never'), images (what picture is missing or a stand-in), noPhotos (true: needs none), about (a plainer summary than its teaches line), note.
When a thread finishes a step for a lesson, change it here (or in the queue it came from) and run npm run status.

clouds.note: The oldest course. Its prose went through several student read-throughs (Oct 2026) and a physics review of the sky lab (3 Nov), but never a Gemini copy edit or a full fact check.

fog.about: What a cloud is made of, how a calm clear night makes fog and stratus, and how rising air builds fair-weather cumulus.

low-sky.about: Stable and unstable air, the lid that flattens heaps into stratocumulus, and why a deep cloud rains when a dark thin one doesn't; nimbostratus.

middle-sky.about: The three height floors, how the Latin names fit together, and three field checks for a cloud's height; altocumulus, cirrocumulus and cirrus.

ice-realm.about: Mares' tails, contrails, the 22° halo and altostratus's frosted sun, read as a warm front's countdown 12 to 24 hours ahead.

giants.about: Latent heat and conditional instability, the morning signs of an afternoon storm, anvils, gust fronts and the 30-30 lightning rule.

front.about: Lows and their fronts, the barometer, why warm fronts soak and cold fronts squall, the crossed-winds rule, and reading rain on radar.

local-sky.about: Rain shadows, standing mountain waves and lens clouds, supercooled water, rime and freezing rain, and how ice crystals make rain.

seeding.about: The 1946 dry ice and silver iodide experiments, which clouds seeding can and can't help, and how randomised trials tested it.

wind.about: How pressure pushes the wind, how the turning Earth bends it along the isobars, friction near the ground, and the jet stream.

coast.about: Why the coast from Seattle to San Francisco hardly ever thunders: a cold sea, a lid of sinking air and the marine layer.

rivers.about: Why the Northwest's rain comes from October to April: the storm track, atmospheric rivers, snow level and the Puget Sound convergence zone.

violent.about: Why a few thunderstorms last all evening and drop big hail: the energy a rising bubble gains, the cap that stores it, and wind shear.

tornado.about: Where a tornado's spin comes from (a horizontal roll tipped up and stretched by an updraft), wall clouds, hook echoes and the EF scale.

hurricane.about: How tropical showers become a hurricane: the trade winds, a heat engine run on warm sea, the eye, what kills one, and storm surge.

winter-fog.about: Why a basin can stay foggy for weeks in winter while the hills are sunny: the cold pool, other kinds of fog, rime and freezing rain.

east-wind.about: Dust walls raised by storms whose rain never lands, and why wind coming down off the Cascades arrives hot and dry; the Gorge and the Santa Ana.
